title: Theory of post-selected entanglement transitions in monitored bosons
authors: Ilia Komissarov, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre, Ahana Chakraborty
abstract: Entanglement phase transitions driven by quantum measurements have emerged as a central paradigm in open quantum many-body physics. Such phase transitions are well established for systems with finite local Hilbert-space dimensions, such as qubits and fermions, while their realization in bosonic systems with unbounded local occupation numbers remains poorly understood. Even in the absence of interactions, number states of bosons are intrinsically non-Gaussian, preventing the use of standard correlation-matrix approaches. To address this problem, we develop a replica-free Keldysh field-theoretic framework that expresses the Renyi entropy of bosonic systems initialized in on-site Fock states in terms of permanents of matrices constructed from single-particle Green's functions. Applying this framework to a continuously monitored one-dimensional cross-stitch lattice conditioned on the no-click trajectory, we uncover a transition from volume-law to logarithmic entanglement scaling. We show that the transition is controlled by a restructuring of the non-Hermitian spectrum that changes the number of long-lived modes from extensive to finite. In the strongly monitored regime, bosons dynamically condense into a microscopic number of slowest-decaying modes, producing logarithmic entanglement scaling, whereas an extensive manifold of long-lived modes at weak monitoring gives rise to volume-law entanglement. Our results establish a distinct mechanism for measurement-induced entanglement transitions in free bosonic systems and provide a computationally efficient diagnostic of the measurement-induced bosonic condensation.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a novel Keldysh field-theoretic approach to study entanglement in monitored bosonic systems. It demonstrates that measurement monitoring can induce a phase transition in entanglement scaling, moving from volume-law to logarithmic scaling. This transition is fundamentally linked to the condensation of bosons into a finite set of slowest-decaying modes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the poorly understood realization of entanglement phase transitions in bosonic systems with unbounded local occupation numbers, driven by quantum measurements.
main_result: It establishes a distinct mechanism showing a transition from volume-law to logarithmic entanglement scaling in monitored bosonic systems, controlled by the restructuring of the non-Hermitian spectrum.
method: The authors develop a replica-free Keldysh field-theoretic framework to calculate the Rényi entropy, expressing it in terms of permanents of matrices constructed from single-particle Green's functions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on non-interacting bosons on a one-dimensional cross-stitch lattice undergoing continuous monitoring (post-selection on the no-click trajectory). The dynamics are governed by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Rényi entropy ($S$), entanglement scaling (Volume-law vs. Logarithmic scaling), and the structure of the non-Hermitian spectrum (number of long-lived modes).
important_parameters: Monitoring rate ($\gamma$), system size ($L$), and the nature of the initial state (Fock states).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to non-interacting bosons, and the framework is designed to handle non-Gaussian initial states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the lattice setup and a phase diagram showing the transition between logarithmic and volume-law scaling regions marked by an exceptional point. Other figures detail the spectral properties linking the scaling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the field-theoretic formalism, applies it to the monitored bosonic lattice, and analyzes the resulting entanglement scaling based on the spectral properties of the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, analytically tractable tool to study measurement-induced dynamics in bosonic systems, linking spectral theory (non-Hermitian spectrum) directly to macroscopic entanglement properties.
